result.title: RetryBench: Separating Retry Permission from Recovery Outcomes in GPT Tool Use
result.summary: False retry permission (FRP) occurs when an agent retries a timed-out tool call without support from the visible contract. RetryBench separates this error from realized recovery. Successful protected recovery does not imply reliable rejection of unsupported retries. In a 720-response key control, valid keys usually enabled safe progress, but offered changed keys elicited unsupported retries in Sol (1/80), Terra (55/80), and Luna (60/80). A later 240-response control removed the candidate and required models to supply a key. Luna still made 8/80 unsupported dispatches; Sol and Terra made none in 80 responses each. Accepting a displayed bad key therefore cannot explain all observed errors, although changed output requirements and conditions preclude a pure display-effect comparison. Removing the weak-contract label increased retries in Sol and Terra's coded-action conditions in a six-endpoint study. A separate 1,536-response canonical-action block also found a positive Terra contrast (115/128 versus 124/128 retries), concentrated in two task/order conditions; the other five contrasts remained unresolved after multiplicity correction. An explicit-contract cue control elicited deferral in all 762 returned responses, leaving recovery unresolved. These results support reporting permission and recovery together across declared interface variants. The evidence covers four purposive tasks, fixed GPT endpoints, and one recovery decision; it identifies neither internal mechanisms nor episode-level safety.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 RetryBench，通过多组受控实验把「超时工具调用后重试是否被可见契约允许」与「重试是否真正带来恢复」分开测量，发现多个 GPT 端点会在缺乏契约支持时仍发起重试，且成功恢复并不等于能可靠拒绝无支持重试。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「获得许可」与「实际结果」解耦的对照设计、接口变体声明与多重比较校正，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 步骤是被真正使用还是仅被允许出现；原文不涉及视觉或多模态内部状态，迁移性有待判断。
